title: Buescher horns in the band; how Phillips got his Martin trumpet
summary: Young gave Phillips a Buescher trumpet for Christmas, which he swapped in Jamestown, North Dakota for a gold Martin; the saxes were Bueschers and the C-melodys Conns.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Yeah. That's where Peggy Lee is from. In Jamestown. So he told me, he says, "I got this horn and I can't play it." He had a gold... Not no gold like they do now. They made gold horns in them days. Burnished gold. And he said it was a Martin. He says, "If you pick up the paint(?) that's on it, you can have it." A horn like that then cost something like about 250 dollars. In them days, that was aa lot of money. He said, "You let me have the Buesher, and I'll owe five more payments on it, but I'm going to lose it because I ain't got the money." He said, "You let me have your horn" and take the payment up. So I just gave him my horn, and I went and paid the payments on it, and got this one, which I got a better deal. So that's how I got the Martin.
But anyway, getting back to the horn, he gave me that horn. In fact, about most everybody in there had Bueshers, all but the saxophones. The C-melodys, they were Conns.
All the other horns that Lester paid were Bueshers.
Except the C-melody, was a Conn.
